title: Archive and Signal
premise: Kestrel Okonkwo has spent eleven years alone tending Earth's abandoned seed vault and its silent beacon, until a derelict ship returns from deep space carrying a crew aged backward into children who remember their own futures. Among them is the ship's former captain, now eight years old, clutching knowledge of a signal that will overwrite every mind on Earth when the last transmission loop completes. Kestrel, the children, and a smuggler they press-gang must cross dead space to the relay that can break the loop, discovering along the way that Kestrel's own forgotten commission was the loop's first link. In the end, Kestrel chooses to stay behind as the relay's living key, sending the found family home while the signal dies with them—justice rendered not by any law, but by inheritance freely given.
about_author: Mara Voss is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete communications technology before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted radio station on the coast, where she still maintains one transmitter 'just in case.'

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Hours
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV establishes the seed vault's rhythms: cataloguing seeds, winding the beacon nobody answers, talking to the dormant AI called Ledger. The emotional beat is loneliness worn smooth into ritual, broken when orbital sensors detect an inbound ship that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: Children of the Long Return
chapters.summary: Kestrel boards the derelict Meridian and finds seven crew members de-aged to childhood, memories intact but bodies wrong. The captain, Iyo, recognizes Kestrel's name and goes pale. POV alternates Kestrel and Iyo; the beat is uncanny tenderness—strangers who know you better than you know yourself.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: Iyo reveals the truth: the beacon Kestrel maintains anchors a transmission loop that will rewrite human memory when it completes—a justice machine built by a vanished court to punish an old atrocity, indiscriminate in its reach. Kestrel's commission papers are the first link. Beat: betrayal by one's own past.

chapters.title: Press-Ganging Providence
chapters.summary: Kestrel trades vault supplies to smuggler Ryn Castellanos for passage, lying about the cargo being children. Ryn's POV shows her recognizing the lie instantly and taking the job anyway—for reasons she won't name. Beat: reluctant alliance, humor against dread.

chapters.title: Dead Space Navigation
chapters.summary: The crossing through dead space where no signals live. The children begin losing future-memories as distance grows from the loop's anchor—Iyo forgets the coordinates she alone knows. Kestrel realizes the beacon can re-anchor them. Beat: grief for a future already slipping away.

chapters.title: The Court That Vanished
chapters.summary: Ledger, awakened remotely, confesses its origin: it served the vanished tribunal, and it chose Kestrel as caretaker because Kestrel's family were the atrocity's victims—the loop was meant to be theirs to arm or disarm. Beat: inheritance as wound; Kestrel rages at being made an instrument.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Small
chapters.summary: The children, terrified of losing themselves, seize the ship and try to turn back toward the loop's comfort. Iyo, youngest and most diminished, must argue her own crew out of surrender. Beat: leadership without authority; the smallest voice carries.

chapters.title: Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: They reach the relay and find it requires a living mind keyed to the original commission—only Kestrel qualifies. Ryn offers to fake the key; Ledger admits no forgery will hold. The transmission loop enters its final cycle. Beat: the trap of being chosen.

chapters.title: Signal and Surrender
chapters.summary: Climax. Kestrel interfaces with the relay to unwind the loop from within, experiencing every memory the punishment would have erased—including their own family's final moments. They choose mercy over verdict, dissolving the loop rather than redirecting it. Beat: justice outside law becomes grace.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Resolution. The relay needs a caretaker; Kestrel stays, beaming seeds and stories outward instead of judgments. Ryn flies the children home to a world that will remember nothing but gain everything. Final image: two beacons, one on Earth, one at the edge, answering each other at last. Beat: found family, kept across distance.
